title: Reliability Gemba Walk Playbook and Team Scripts
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, lightweight playbook for running cross-functional Reliability Gemba Walks focused on translating product-level SLAs into service-level SLOs and actionable remediation experiments. Goal is to create fast alignment, surface latent operational risks, and seed 30/60/90 day experiments that reduce error budget burn and latency hotspots.

When to use this playbook:
- Kickoff for a service or feature going to canary or wide rollout
- After a major incident where root causes span infra + product + ML model layers
- Quarterly SLO refresh / owner onboarding across teams

Core principles (how we run these):
1) Observational first: start with real metrics (dashboards, traces, recent incidents) and let data lead conversations.
2) Issue-to-experiment bias: every observation should map to at least one hypothesis-driven experiment (30/60/90).
3) Short scripts, clear roles: rotates facilitator, scribe, technical lead, product owner.
4) Low overhead artifacts: 1 pager per experiment + a single decision log entry.

Pre-walk checklist (owners in parentheses):
- Deck: 3 slides: current SLO, last 30-day burn, top 3 error categories (SRE)
- Live dashboards: latency P50/P95/P99, error rates by route, infra saturation graphs (Monitoring)
- Incident index: list of Sev2+ in last 90 days with short impact summary (SRE)
- Model/feature notes: known model regressions, prompt/temperature changes in last 30 days (Applied ML/Product)
- Invite list: SRE lead, infra engineer, product manager, applied-ML rep, console/observability owner, a solutions-engineer (Organizer)

Roles and a 12-step facilitation script (45-60 minutes):
- Facilitator (F): keeps time, ensures agenda, surfaces next steps.
- Scribe (S): captures findings in decision log + creates experiment stubs in Jira.
- Technical Lead (TL): answers deep questions, commits to follow-ups.
- Product Owner (PO): clarifies user impact and rollout plans.

1. Opening (5 min, F): objective of this walk, clarify scope and expected outcome (1–3 experiments + owner assignments).
2. Quick context (5 min, SRE): top-line SLOs and current burn.
3. Live snapshot (10 min, Monitoring): show P95 trends, error-rate heatmap, and host/GPU pressure. Keep to 3 visuals.
4. Incident highlights (5 min, SRE): two short incident summaries, why they matter for SLOs.
5. Product/model changes (5 min, PO/Applied ML): list recent rollouts or model swaps that could change signal.
6. Walk the traces (10 min, TL + Monitoring): pick 1–2 representative slow/error traces; walk the group through them.
7. Brain-dump constraints (5 min, cross-team): what ops/product/infra gating exists for fixes?
8. Hypothesis generation (5 min, cross-team): rapid capture: cause -> experiment -> success metric.
9. Prioritize experiments (5 min, F + PO): pick top 3 by impact / feasibility.
10. Experiment definition (10 min, Scribe + TL): for each top experiment capture: owner, brief plan, measurement, rollback criteria, Jira stub id.
11. Communication plan (3 min, PO): how we notify stakeholders and customers if experiment alters behavior (e.g., fallback model).
12. Close (2 min, F): confirm owners and next sync time (usually 1 week).

Templates (cut-and-paste into Jira / Confluence):
- Experiment 1-pager (title, owner, hypothesis, change to be made, metric to measure, success threshold, rollout window, rollback criteria, stakeholders)
- Decision Log entry (date, decision summary, rationale, owners, experiment link, expected review date)

Example experiment stubs (realistic but fictional):
- 30-day: "Reduce per-route P95 by prefilling KV cache for chat-start flows" (owner: Miguel T)
  - Hypothesis: high cold-start KV cache misses cause 20–30% P95 spikes for chat-start; prefill will reduce thread initialization latency.
  - Metric: chat-start P95, error% during startup window.
  - Success: 15% reduction in P95, no increase in errors.

- 60-day: "Route lower-importance embed requests to quantized model pool during peak" (owner: Priya N)
  - Hypothesis: offloading background embedding jobs will reduce tail latency for high-priority generation by reducing contention.
  - Metric: cross-queue tail latency, CPU/GPU utilization.
  - Success: measurable tail latency improvement on high-priority queue without quality regression.

30/60/90 experiment cadence and governance:
- 30-day: quick wins and safety-net guards (feature flags, small traffic slices). Review in weekly SLO sync.
- 60-day: medium complexity experiments (model routing policies, persistent caching tweaks). Review in SLO review meeting.
- 90-day: larger infra changes or rollout (reserved capacity reshuffle, autoscaler policy adjustments). Gate with product and platform leads.

Escalation and rollback rules:
- Any experiment that increases error rate > threshold (configured per SLO) must be immediately rolled back by owner and SRE notified.
- If an experiment touches private deployments or KMS, follow the Private Deployments change protocol and notify security.

Artifacts to produce after each walk (owner in parens):
- Decision log entry (Scribe)
- Up to 3 Jira experiment tickets with measurable success criteria (Scribe + TL)
- Short status note to exec stakeholders: 3 bullets (PO)
- Telemetry checklist for measurement (Monitoring)

Risk matrix (quick):
- Risk: model quality regression. Mitigation: A/B evaluation on 1% traffic, canary to 5% then 25%.
- Risk: infra capacity shock. Mitigation: pre-reserve burst capacity, define fallback model pool.
- Risk: cross-team coordination delays. Mitigation: pre-assign owners and require 48h pre-walk artifacts.

30/60/90 example calendar (minimal cadence):
- Day 0: Gemba Walk (playbook used), experiments created
- Day 7: Quick check-in (are experiments running? early signals?)
- Day 30: 30-day review, decide continue/rollback/scale
- Day 60: 60-day review (progress + extend to larger rollouts)
- Day 90: Post-mortem / consolidation: fold successful experiments into runbooks and SLO guardrails

Communication snippets (copy/paste):
- Meeting invite subject: "Reliability Gemba Walk — [service-name] — Focus: SLO translation & 30/60/90 experiments"
- Stakeholder update email: "Summary: 2 experiments created to address chat-start P95 and embedding contention. Owners: Miguel T, Priya N. Next sync: 2026-03-05."

Checklist for SLO translation (quick):
- Map customer-facing SLA -> internal SLO(s) (request-level latency, error-rate, freshness)
- Ensure measurement windows match user impact patterns (e.g., peak minutes vs 24h)
- Define per-route burn alarms and escalation steps
- Capture quality guardrails (model evaluation tests tied to rollout policy)

Appendix: Quick facilitation tips
- Keep slides to max 3 visuals; show data, not narrative.
- Use a parking-lot for long technical debates; convert to async follow-up with owner.
- Rotate facilitator every 4 walks to spread institutional knowledge.

Open questions (for the reliability program team to decide):
- Should we require a pre-walk canary checklist for all experiments touching model routing? (PO + Applied ML input needed)
- How do we tie experiment outcomes to cost tradeoffs (ops/finance input needed)?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft a lightweight Confluence template for the Decision Log (Aisha)
- Prototype a shared dashboard filter for "Gemba Walk snapshot" (Sofia)
- Run pilot with two product teams in March and capture feedback (Daniel)

End of doc.
